ground_truth.title: The Climate Tech Marketing Starter Pack
ground_truth.author: Sean Higgins
ground_truth.main_content:
How to tell your story without sounding like every other climate company

Hey there! 👋

Skander here.

Building climate solutions are hard. Selling them might be even harder.

You’ve got the science. You’ve got the prototype. Maybe you’ve even got the first customer. But when it comes to explaining what you actually do - to investors, to partners, to your next hire - most climate founders still fumble the mic.

Too much jargon. Too many buzzwords. Not enough why this matters, right now.

This Starter Pack is Sean’s crash course in climate storytelling that actually works, just in time for o ur Open Climate session next week Wednesday at 9am PST | 18:00 CEST. Register here, places are limited as always so we can have an actual conversation on how to market better:

Register Now

As always we broke it down into levels:

Beginner: Fix your website. Learn to message like a human.

Intermediate: Navigate the shifting language of climate, politics, and perception.

Expert: Build trust, consistency, and long-term narrative firepower.

🌊 Let’s dive in

But first, who is Sean?

Sean Higgins is a freelance content and messaging strategist with 15 years of experience in B2B writing. He has worked with big tech companies like Boston Dynamics, Contentful, and PTC, helping them tell strong stories about their complex technologies using blog posts, case studies, web copy, and other written content.

Last year, he (finally) admitted that the climate emergency was not going away and decided to do something about it. Now he collaborates with climate-tech companies to build the story that communicates their value quickly — so they can stop worrying about “telling a better story” and get back to more important work.

Beginner: How do I sell my solution better?

Climate-Tech Messaging is Dead, Here’s How to Tell a Better Story

Do prospects and investors read your website and still ask, What does your company do, and why should I care? Read this first.

My guide argues that the strongest messaging strategy for your climate-tech website or pitch deck is to drop all the aspirational stuff and just explain the value your technology offers. Like a human, using specific, straightforward language. Read it and you’ll learn what good messaging looks like, and how to use the jobs to be done framework to build it yourself.

Climate Tech Comms for VC Fundraising in 2025

Tell the Future argues that effective messaging is just the first step in securing investors for your climate tech. You also need to master “storytelling across multiple formats and lengthy timeframes.” Lucky for you, that’s easier than it seems: The writers got in touch with VCs from MCJ, Pale Blue Dot, and other leading firms to share actionable advice about understanding your investors, tailoring your approach, and avoiding the most common pitfalls.

Anti-Greenwashing Guide

One ultra-important factor in your marketing and storytelling: tell the truth. That means taking care to build a value prop that your tech can actually deliver — it also means not exaggerating your climate claims. This guide from Creatives for Climate offers tactical steps you can take to keep greenwashing out of your messaging and storytelling. (A big one: Verify your claims with real scientific evidence.)

The guide is written for agency creatives, but the advice is so clear and easy to follow that it should be required reading for anyone in climate.

👉 https://issuu.com/creativesforclimate/docs/ethical_agency_handbook_for_agencies/10

Intermediate: Can we even call ourselves “climate tech” anymore?

RIP ‘climate tech’

This hot take from Sifted features insights from investors at leading firms who argue that “climate tech” was only ever a VC label to describe investment strategies, not a meaningful description of an industry, or even a market. The takeaway? The term “climate-tech” needs to go away, and fast.

👉 https://sifted.eu/articles/rip-dead-climate-tech

How to reassess your cleantech comms strategy in an uncertain policy landscape

In today’s political “climate” (sorry), using words like “carbon,” “net-zero,” or even “green” can feel like a risk. So what DO we call our companies? It depends. This guide from climate-tech comms agency DG+ will show you how to answer that question for yourself, step by step. It covers steps you can take to consider broader political trends, decide what’s right for your team, get internal alignment, adapt your messaging, and more.

👉 https://heatmap.news/culture/branding-energy-dominance

Risk Management Might Save Climate Tech

If the idea of branding your climate solution as something other than climate-tech feels like capitulating to an inclement politics, check this piece. It argues that “climate change is just one problem among many,” and probably not the one that will be most convincing to your prospects or investors.

Instead, companies should focus on what their audience actually cares about — risk management. These times are tumultuous for your customers, too. Why not sell yourself as a way to prepare for an uncertain future?

Expert: A value prop is great, but how do we tell our story in the long term?

Dear Marketers: Should your Founder be an Influencer (on LinkedIn)?

The data is conclusive: sharing your founder’s thought-leadership on LinkedIn is, by far, the most effective way to engage your audience and raise your profile. But in 2025, posting on social media is a fraught proposition — How can you adopt this strategy without adding more AI slop and warmed-over insight to an already noisy platform?

Short answer: Listen to this podcast. Over an hour, three veteran marketers cover tactical issues like deciding whether the strategy is right for you, building a presence over time, and writing content people actually want to read.

Corporate Authenticity in the Era of Polarization

“It’s not enough to have polished messaging,” this data-rich article argues. With a boatload of statistics, it makes the case that companies can’t rely on their value prop to land customers and investors. They also can’t simply plug into a broader trend like “national security” or “energy resilience” and call it a day. In 2025 and beyond, this piece argues, all companies must be clear about the values they champion and stick to them. Even in B2B, even in climate tech.

👉 https://www.robroyconsulting.com/perspectives/corporate-authenticity

Seven Lessons from 25 Years of Telling Climate Stories

Launchsquad has been telling climate-tech stories for a quarter of a century, and they’ve learned a thing or two. This piece offers a bite-size master class in the nuances of telling a better story, selling your vision to an array of stakeholders, and proving your impact. The most surprising takeaway? Kicking B2B marketing dogma to the curb can have some tremendous upsides in climate comms.

👉 https://launchsquad.com/blog-library/25anniversaryclimate
